children: Cloudflare
is expanding its cybersecurity arsenal with
Adaptive Intelligence

, a new AI-powered threat detection engine designed to stop automated attacks before they can scale. The launch strengthens Cloudflare's push into AI-driven security at a time when bots are becoming faster and cheaper to deploy, potentially giving the company another way to monetize the rapid growth of machine-generated internet traffic.

Cloudflare provides internet infrastructure and cybersecurity services that help businesses protect websites, applications and networks while improving performance. Its products include content delivery, bot management, network security and developer tools, with customers paying for access to its global cloud platform.
Adaptive Intelligence is being integrated into Cloudflare's Bot Management platform and is designed to detect threats such as
credential stuffing, automated scraping and other bot-driven attacks
Unlike traditional security systems that rely heavily on static rules, the engine continuously analyzes live traffic and automatically generates
short-lived defensive rules
as attackers change tactics. Cloudflare says this makes attacks harder to repeat and increases the cost of continuously modifying malicious bots.

The timing is important because AI is lowering the technical barrier for attackers to build and adapt sophisticated automated campaigns. That dynamic could increase demand for cybersecurity platforms capable of adjusting without waiting for manual updates.
Cloudflare already enters the launch with strong growth momentum. Second-quarter revenue rose
36% year over year to $696.1 million
, while current remaining performance obligations grew
, indicating continued strength in contracted future revenue. Free cash flow reached
$56.4 million
, or 8% of revenue.
Investor Takeaway
For Cloudflare investors, the key question is whether Adaptive Intelligence becomes another meaningful driver of enterprise security spending rather than simply a product enhancement.
Investors should watch
large-customer growth, security product adoption, current RPO and revenue growth
for evidence that customers are spending more to defend against AI-enabled threats.

Cloudflare's 36% revenue growth provides a strong starting point, but continued investment in AI security must eventually support improving margins and cash generation. If automated attacks accelerate, Cloudflare's ability to analyze traffic across its global network could become an increasingly valuable competitive advantage.

title: Cloudflare Makes Bigger AI Push as Threats Rise
